newsitem.title: UK: First Choice says outlook encouraging.
newsitem.headline: First Choice says outlook encouraging.

text.p: British tour operator First Choice Holidays Plc said on Wednesday net summer bookings at March 22 were up 21 percent on the year earlier, representing 59 percent of its targeted full season sales.

The company said in a statement for its annual general meeting that the outlook for the year was encouraging and in line with its expectations. It said progress to date suggested improved full-year performance.

"In particular, the higher percentage of our British summer 1997 on sale capacity already sold means that we enter the important late sales market in a far stronger position than last year," chairman Michael Julien said.

First Choice said net winter holiday bookings were down nine percent as of March 22 in line with its move to cut the number of holidays offered by 10 percent. It said it lost market share in winter holidays but margins on bookings were higher.
First Choice said the integration of its existing ski business with newly-acquired SkiBound was progressing well but Signature Vacations in Canada was hit by weak demand and overcapacity.
Bookings were down seven percent and Signature Vacations was expected to contribute less in the first half than a year earlier.

"In summary, the adverse conditions in Canada have offset the better British performance and there is unlikely to be a reduction in the Winter loss for the current year. However, it remains our intention to progressively reduce this loss by further enhancing margins through increased operating efficiencies," First Choice said.
